proof:
Source: (1a)–(1c) of the parent proof, stated for an arbitrary measure finite on compacts and a constant n-vector.

1. Integrability. μ is finite on compact sets (an IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts instance built from the hypothesis). Let ω ∈ D^n(U): ω is C^∞ with compact support. The function f_ω(x) := w(ω(x)) is continuous (w is a continuous linear map and ω is continuous) and has compact support, because w(0) = 0 (HasCompactSupport.comp_left). A continuous compactly supported function is integrable for a measure finite on compacts (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport). So f_ω is μ-integrable.

2. Linearity. Define L(ω) := ∫ f_ω dμ for ω ∈ D^n(U). Since forms add and scale pointwise and w is linear, f_{ω+η} = f_ω + f_η and f_{rω} = r·f_ω. By step 1 and integral_add, L(ω + η) = L(ω) + L(η); by integral_const_mul, L(rω) = r·L(ω). So L is a linear functional on D^n(U).

3. Sequential continuity. Let ω_j → 0 in D^n(U) (TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0). Then there is a compact K with tsupport ω_j ⊆ K for every j, and the 0-th iterated derivatives of ω_j converge uniformly on K to the 0-th iterated derivative of the zero form, which is 0. Since ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 f x‖ = ‖f(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero), for every r > 0 we have ‖ω_j(x)‖ < r for all x ∈ K and all large j. Let ε > 0, put m_K := (μ(K)).toReal (finite by hypothesis) and C := ‖w‖·m_K + 1 > 0, and take j so large that ‖ω_j(x)‖ < ε/C for all x ∈ K. Since tsupport ω_j ⊆ K, ω_j(x) = 0 for every x ∉ K (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport), so f_{ω_j} vanishes off K and ∫ f_{ω_j} dμ = ∫_K f_{ω_j} dμ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero). For x ∈ K, |f_{ω_j}(x)| ≤ ‖w‖·‖ω_j(x)‖ ≤ ‖w‖·ε/C (ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm). Hence (norm_setIntegral_le_of_norm_le_const, μ(K) < ∞) |L(ω_j)| ≤ ‖w‖·(ε/C)·m_K = ε·(‖w‖·m_K)/C < ε. Thus L(ω_j) → 0.

4. Conclusion. T := (L, step 3) is a GeometricCurrentOn U n. By definition T(ω) = ∫ w(ω(x)) dμ(x), and the integrand is μ-integrable by step 1; this is exactly IsMeasureRepresentation T μ (fun _ => w). ∎
key_steps: For ω ∈ D^n(U), x ↦ w(ω(x)) is continuous with compact support, hence μ-integrable.
L(ω) := ∫ w(ω) dμ is linear (integral_add, integral_const_mul).
If ω_j → 0 in D^n(U), supports lie in one compact K and sup_K ‖ω_j‖ → 0, so |L(ω_j)| ≤ ‖w‖·μ(K)·sup_K‖ω_j‖ → 0.
T := (L, continuity) is a current and (μ, const w) represents it by construction.
